zh.headline: Claude Fable 5 全球恢复访问
zh.observation: 今天最明确的信号是：**AI 行业正在从"模型能力竞赛"转向"Agent 实用化争夺"**。Zuckerberg 坦承 Agent 进展不及预期，微软砸 25 亿美元做深度部署，而 OpenAI、Anthropic 则加速自研芯片以降低成本——这些看似分散的消息都指向同一个方向：让 AI 真正在企业和开发者手中产生价值，比训练下一个 SOTA 模型更难，也更重要。同时，开源生态的 Agent 工具链（Chrome DevTools MCP、Agent 技能框架、多路复用器等）正在快速成熟，为下一波 Agent 应用爆发打下基础设施。值得注意的是，Fable 5 回归后的"信任 Agent 判断力"讨论，可能预示着人机协作方式的一个根本性转变。

items.title: Fable 5 的"判断力"使用技巧

en.headline: Claude Fable 5 Restored Globally
en.observation: The clearest signal today: **the AI industry is shifting from "model capability competition" to "agent practicalization battle."** Zuckerberg admits agent progress is slower than expected, Microsoft invests $2.5B in deep deployment, while OpenAI and Anthropic accelerate self-chip efforts to reduce costs—these seemingly scattered messages all point in the same direction: making AI truly deliver value in enterprise and developer hands is harder and more important than training the next SOTA model. Meanwhile, the open-source agent tooling ecosystem (Chrome DevTools MCP, agent skill frameworks, multiplexers, etc.) is rapidly maturing, laying infrastructure for the next wave of agent application explosion. Notably, the "trust agent judgement" discussion following Fable 5's return may signal a fundamental shift in human-AI collaboration paradigms.

items.title: AI Coding Addiction Controversy
items.desc: LeadDev article and Hacker News debate the addictive nature of AI coding assistants—engineers over-relying on AI-generated code leads to reduced understanding depth and tech debt accumulation. Simon Willison at AIE conference cited Geoffrey Litt's "understand to participate" framing, emphasizing the need to maintain code understanding depth when collaborating with coding agents to avoid cognitive debt.

items.title: Fable 5's "Use Your Judgement" Technique
items.desc: At the AIE conference, Claude Code team members suggested letting Fable (and Opus) use their own judgement rather than manually specifying every detail. For example, in testing strategy, telling the model "use your judgement" works better than detailed rules on when to run tests. This perspective sparked widespread discussion in the developer community, reflecting the rise of a new paradigm of "trusting agent judgement."
